name: clay
description: Clay enrichment and custom functions — official MCP server (OAuth with dynamic client registration) plus Public API routines

requirements: OAuth 2.0 client that supports Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) — PKCE is mandatory
Clay API key (header clay-api-key) if you use the Public API alternative
notes: MCP endpoint https://api.clay.com/v3/mcp; dynamic client registration at https://api.clay.com/oauth/register.
Scope mcp; access tokens live 1h and refresh tokens rotate.
Authorization https://app.clay.com/oauth/authorize, token https://api.clay.com/oauth/token, revoke https://api.clay.com/oauth/revoke.

Public API alternative: POST https://api.clay.com/public/v0/routines/{routine_id}/run with header clay-api-key, then GET .../routines/run/{routine_run_id}/results (202 while processing, 200 when complete, per-item status).
Running a function by id requires that function's MCP access to be enabled in Clay settings.
Admins control the 'Allowed MCP clients' list and per-user / per-role credit budgets; credits are consumed at the same rate as in-app work.
The MCP endpoint returns an Mcp-Session-Id header on initialize — echo it on every subsequent call. Skipping it is the most common Clay integration failure.
Dynamic client registration is open and self-service but rate-limited (burst 4, refill ~10 per hour per IP).
Admin policy is re-checked at token issuance, so revoking an allowed client can 401 an otherwise working connection on the next refresh.
Dry-run: run a workflow in test mode; generated email/SMS is saved as a draft before send. MCP cannot send campaign emails from the Sequencer, but one-off sends are callable.
